body: That's not a good idea, because it would share pass-by-reference types like `Array`. The default value needs to be constructed from scratch.
Couldn't I just solve it with `.duplicate(true)`? Correct me if wrong

Ah wait you are using `member_default_values`, I was thinking about `member_default_values_cache` (for which `duplicate(true)` would get rid of unwanted pass-by-ref, but it would also destroy intended linkage e.g. `var a = []; var b = [a]`).
I'm not that familiar with the properties of this one since it's unused at the moment, see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111171

From a skim it seems like it only stores stuff that can be constant folded, so it might be a valid stop gap solution, but IMO the end goal would be to actually run dynamic initializers when hot reloading (that might be pretty involved though).

Will have to look into this a bit more.

Feel free to let me know when you've taken a look and we can discuss in contributors chat if you want. I'm willing to put in the time to make the optimal solution + I'm interested in learning about the engine internals, tho I might need some guidance.

Ok in my mind there are two things we need to address here:

1. After a hot reload the script instance state must be compatible with the typing of the variables.
   - This is pretty high priority since it can lead to crashes (real crashes not the ones that the GDScript debugger can catch).
   - This does not only effect newly added variables (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/124352)

2. After a hot reload the script instance state of added stuff should match as accurately as possible with a freshly created instance.
   - Definitely something we want, but not as high prio as the other thing because all issues that can be caused by this are catchable by the debugger.
   - This one might make sense to split further on a technical level:
      1. Respecting pure initializer e.g. `var a: int = 1`
         - By pure I mean initializer that don't rely on other functions or members 
         - For those handling arrays and dicts with `duplicate` should be fine.
         - As far as I can tell that's basically what `member_default_values` does right now, might need some more testing though, that I've not had time for yet.
      2. Respecting dynamic initializers
         - Haven't given it further thought. But absolutely can be tackled later.

I'd say addressing `2.a` is probably better suited for 4.9 at this point (especially since `member_default_values` isn't battle tested), while a  fix for `1` would still be valid for 4.8 IMO (simpler and more urgent). I'll leave it up to you if you want to continue on 2.a, or trim this down to just ensuring types and doing a followup.

In any case this must work the same for all `DEBUG_ENABLED` builds (those are the builds with hot reload support). An `TOOLS_ENABLED` in the impl is bound to lead to inconsistencies that I'd like to avoid. Given that `member_default_values` is unused you should be able to just move it to `DEBUG_ENABLED`.
